hearing.title: Senate Committee on Finance: CSO Budget Consultation - October 26, 2026

segments.speaker: Senator Joseph Victor "JV" G. Ejercito
segments.text: The consultation of the Committee on Finance, Subcommittee A, with civil society organizations to discuss budgetary priorities for the proposed fiscal year 2027 budget is hereby called to order. I'd like to acknowledge the presence of our colleague, Senator Panfilo Lacson.

segments.speaker: Senator Joseph Victor "JV" G. Ejercito
segments.text: And before we recognize the resource persons, the Chair would like to state some guidelines for our orderly conduct for this afternoon. Due to the limited number of seats available at the panel, only one resource person per CSO will be seated at the panel. Should a question be addressed or answered by your colleague, you must first seek the permission of the Chair to have your colleague recognized before they may respond.

segments.speaker: Senator Joseph Victor "JV" G. Ejercito
segments.text: We would like also to remind everyone that each CSO is allotted a maximum of five minutes to deliver its statement or presentation. A timer will be displayed on the screen to help everyone keep track of their allotted time. Thank you for your understanding and cooperation. We welcome our partners from civil society organizations and all our guests for today's discussions. At this juncture, may I request the Committee Secretary to acknowledge the resource persons present for today.

segments.speaker: Committee Secretary
segments.text: Thank you, Mr. Chair. Good afternoon. Good afternoon also to Senator Lacson. For the consultation with civil society organizations to discuss budgetary priorities for the FY 2027 General Appropriations Act or GAA, we would like to acknowledge our resource persons.

segments.speaker: Committee Secretary
segments.text: First, from the People's Budget Coalition, we have Mr. Kenneth Isaiah Ibasco Abante together with Ms. Zy-za Nadine Suzara, Mr. Adolfo Jose Montesa and Ms. Maxine Valdez. For GoodGovPH, we have Mr. Michel Andre Macahilo. From Social Watch Philippines, we have Dr. Maria Victoria Raquiza, who is also a professor of UP NCPAG, together with Mr. Alci Kitalig and Ms. Desiree Peña-Flor. From the Caucus of Development NGO Networks or CODE-NGO, we have Ms. Catherine Basalote together with Ms. Samantha May Santos and Mr. Lawrence Kenneth Castillo.

segments.speaker: Committee Secretary
segments.text: From Citizen Watch Philippines, we have Ms. Julia Christine Baza. From Democracy Watch Philippines, we have Mr. Lloyd Ian Zaragoza. From FOI Youth Initiative or FYI, we have Mr. Aljon Patrick Acupan. From Action for Economic Reforms, we have Atty. Paula Mae Tanquieng together with Ms. Roshek Sims and Ms. Emily Joy Capule. From the Samahan ng Nagkakaisang Pamilya ng Pantawid or SNPP, we have Ms. Annabelle Luna together with Ms. Jeana Catacio.

segments.speaker: Committee Secretary
segments.text: From World Vision Philippines, we have Ms. Pauline Navarro. From Unang Hakbang Foundation, Inc., we have Ms. Mary Aieen Padoga. From E-Net Philippines, we have Prof. Flora Arellano together with Ms. Mercy Mitsichan. From the Center for Youth Advocacy and Networking or CYAN or Multiply-Ed, we have Mr. Humphrey Soriano together with Ms. Isaiah Sosa and Ms. Krista Nicole Buat. From the Ateneo Center for Research and Innovation or ACRI, we have Dr. Geminn Louis Apostol together with Dr. Theo Prudencio Juhani Capeding.

segments.speaker: Committee Secretary
segments.text: From the Medical Action Group or MAG and UHC Collective, we have Dr. Juan Antonio Perez III, who is also the former Undersecretary for Population Development Integration of the CPD. From the Healthcare Professionals Alliance Against COVID-19 or HPAAC, we have Dr. Alberto Ong Jr. From the Philippine Alliance of Patient Organizations or PAPO, we have Ms. Arsenia Torres. From the Youth for Health Coalition, we have Ms. Aliyah May Lozari and Ms. Arriane dela Cruz. From the Youth for Mental Health Coalition or Y4MH, we have Ms. Ray Alyannah Ysabel Lagasca.

segments.speaker: Committee Secretary
segments.text: From the Filipino Sign Language National Network or FSLN2, we have Dr. Liza Martinez. From the Philippine Anti-Discrimination Alliance of Youth Leaders or PANTAY, we have Mr. Aaron James Villapando. From Aksyon Klima Pilipinas or AKP, we have Mr. John Leo Algo and Ms. Martha Balagal. From Magsasaka at Siyentipiko para sa Pag-unlad ng Agrikultura or MASIPAG, we have Ms. Ira Angela Domingo and Mr. John Althani Famador.

segments.speaker: Committee Secretary
segments.text: That's it, Mr. Chair. I'm sorry. We also have representatives from the Move As One Coalition: Mr. Luisito Hepuela and Dr. Maureen Ava Mata. From Renacimiento Manila, Ms. Bea Dolores together with Mr. Crisostomo Miguel Ordonez III and Mr. Matthew Gabriel Caudal. And last but not the least, from the Public Services Labor Independent Confederation or PSLink, Dr. Annie Enriquez-Geron. Thank you, Mr. Chair.

segments.speaker: Senator Joseph Victor "JV" G. Ejercito
segments.text: Thank you, Comsec. Magandang araw po sa ating lahat, lalo na sa ating mga kasamahan sa Senado at sa ating mga katuwang mula sa civil society organizations. Every peso we allocate represents a choice about the kind of future we want for our people. These choices must be informed by the experiences of the communities we serve. This is why your participation in the budget process matters.

segments.speaker: Senator Joseph Victor "JV" G. Ejercito
segments.text: Noong nakaraang taon, nagsagawa ng konsultasyon sa mga civil society organizations ang ating Senate President Sherwin Gatchalian, na noon ay chairperson ng Committee on Finance. We recognize the foundation he laid for greater public participation in our budget deliberations. Under our chairmanship, we kept building on that effort by bringing your participation directly into the budget hearings.

segments.speaker: Senator Joseph Victor "JV" G. Ejercito
segments.text: Sinulatan natin ang mga vice chairperson ng Committee on Finance upang mabigyan ng puwang ang mga CSO sa mga pagdinig ng kanilang mga subcommittee. May ilang vice chairperson natin na nag-imbita ng mga CSO at iba pang grupo upang makaupo sa mga hearing at maibahagi ang kanilang mga pananaw sa mga panukalang budget ng mga ahensya.

segments.speaker: Senator Joseph Victor "JV" G. Ejercito
segments.text: We also invited you to submit questions that we could raise on your behalf. Sinama natin ang inyong mga tanong at alalahanin sa pagbusisi ng budget ng bawat ahensya. Ipinadala rin natin ang mga ito sa mga kinauukulang departamento upang mabigyan ng kaukulang pansin, sagot at aksyon. We want your participation to have a meaningful place in the scrutiny of the proposed budgets of our national government

segments.speaker: Senator Joseph Victor "JV" G. Ejercito
segments.text: agencies, in the questions officials are asked to answer and in the priorities we put forward. Mahalaga ang inyong ambag dahil marami sa inyo ang direktang nakikipag-ugnayan sa mga komunidad. Your experience helps us to achieve our goal of going back to basics. As we prepare our 2027 budget, you help us assess whether the proposed allocations respond to the actual needs of the people.

segments.speaker: Senator Joseph Victor "JV" G. Ejercito
segments.text: Today, we are also working to make budget information more accessible and useful to the public. Kasalukuyan nating isinusulong ang pagsasama sa Senate Budget Transparency Portal ng ilan sa mga tools ng ating mga katuwang, kabilang ang People's Budget Coalition at Better Gov PH. Through this effort, we hope to bring these tools to a wider audience and help more Filipinos understand, examine and monitor the national budget. Transparency is more felt when people can actually use the information to ask questions and hold their government accountable.

segments.speaker: Senator Joseph Victor "JV" G. Ejercito
segments.text: We're applying the same commitment to transparency in our scrutiny of the proposed DPWH budget na tumaas ng higit P11.49 billion sa ilalim ng General Appropriations Bill. Mula sa 11,420 projects under the 2027 NEP, lumaki rin po ang kabuuang bilang ng mga proyekto sa 16,244 sa ilalim ng GAB.

segments.speaker: Senator Joseph Victor "JV" G. Ejercito
segments.text: Kapansin-pansin din po sa aming pagsusuri ang paglobo ng pondo sa ilalim ng DPWH Convergence Program tulad ng mga multipurpose buildings at basic infrastructure projects na umabot sa P74 billion. Samantala, binawasan ng higit P73 billion ang pondo para sa malalaking foreign-assisted projects na importante sa pagpapalago ng ating ekonomiya. Ito rin ang dahilan kung kaya bumuo tayo ng isang dedicated na team na nakatutok lamang sa masusing line-by-line review ng NEP at General Appropriations Bill mula sa Kamara.

segments.speaker: Senator Joseph Victor "JV" G. Ejercito
segments.text: Sinuri po natin ang mga pagbabago sa nakalaang pondo at bilang ng mga proyekto, ang kanilang mga supporting documents at kung may repetition o pag-uulit sa mga proyektong may nakalaang pondo sa kasalukuyang budget. Our initial review has flagged about P266 billion worth of projects for further scrutiny and review, including concerns over the supporting documents submitted to the Committee.

segments.speaker: Senator Joseph Victor "JV" G. Ejercito
segments.text: Of the 16,244 total projects under the DPWH operations budget, only 1,418 projects, or 8.73%, were submitted with accompanying physical or digital documentation. A staggering 14,826 projects, or 91.27%, had no submitted supporting documents.

segments.speaker: Senator Joseph Victor "JV" G. Ejercito
segments.text: Kasama rin po dito ang 23 line items na may laang pondo sa ilalim ng 2026 General Appropriations Act na may kabuuang halaga ng P227.2 million. We also note several lump-sum line items worth P20.5 billion under the GAB. These findings require clear explanations from the DPWH at mahalaga na bago tayo maglaan ng pondo, malinaw ang batayan, pangangailangan at dokumentasyon ng bawat proyekto.

segments.speaker: Senator Joseph Victor "JV" G. Ejercito
segments.text: Beyond this year's budget review, we want these reforms to endure beyond one's chairmanship, Senate Committee on Finance or budget cycle. Kaya po ngayong araw, bago ang pagbubukas ng konsultasyon na ito kasama ang civil society organizations at government watchdogs, naghahain tayo ng tatlong panukalang batas upang mapagtibay at gawing mas makabuluhan ang pakikilahok ng ating mga mamamayan sa pagbabalangkas, pamamahala at paglalaan ng pondo ng bayan.

segments.speaker: Senator Joseph Victor "JV" G. Ejercito
segments.text: First, the Bantay Budget Act or Senate Bill No. 2576, which seeks to institutionalize CSO participation in the preparation and authorization of the budget. It provides avenues for you to submit proposals, participate in budget hearings and access budget documents, including records of bicameral conference proceedings. Second, the Grassroots Participatory Budgeting Act or Senate Bill No. 2577 seeks

segments.speaker: Senator Joseph Victor "JV" G. Ejercito
segments.text: to bring community-identified priorities into local and national budgeting.

Social Watch Philippines Co-convenor Dr. Maria Victoria Raquiza
segments.text: On behalf of Social Watch Philippines,

segments.speaker: Social Watch Philippines Co-convenor Dr. Maria Victoria Raquiza
segments.text: I will present our assessment of the proposed

segments.speaker: Social Watch Philippines Co-convenor Dr. Maria Victoria Raquiza
segments.text: 2027 Budget to the Lens of Social Equity and Human Rights.

segments.speaker: Social Watch Philippines Co-convenor Dr. Maria Victoria Raquiza
segments.text: My colleagues around the table will subsequently elaborate

segments.speaker: Social Watch Philippines Co-convenor Dr. Maria Victoria Raquiza
Social Watch Philippines Co-convenor Dr. Maria Victoria Raquiza
Social Watch Philippines Co-convenor Dr. Maria Victoria Raquiza
segments.text: the proposed 2027 budget raises a number of serious concerns.

segments.speaker: Social Watch Philippines Co-convenor Dr. Maria Victoria Raquiza
segments.text: First, the apparent failure to prioritize the productive sectors,

segments.speaker: Social Watch Philippines Co-convenor Dr. Maria Victoria Raquiza
Social Watch Philippines Co-convenor Dr. Maria Victoria Raquiza
segments.text: which historically has been getting very low public investments,

segments.speaker: Social Watch Philippines Co-convenor Dr. Maria Victoria Raquiza
segments.text: and it is even lower this year.

segments.speaker: Social Watch Philippines Co-convenor Dr. Maria Victoria Raquiza
segments.text: These are critical to raising productivity, generating decent employment, and improving people's incomes.

segments.speaker: Social Watch Philippines Co-convenor Dr. Maria Victoria Raquiza
segments.text: The 2027 proposed budget raises debt service, public works, the defense sector, law and order, while significantly cutting the budget for agriculture, agrarian reform, and trade and industry.

segments.speaker: Social Watch Philippines Co-convenor Dr. Maria Victoria Raquiza
segments.text: These are the productivity-enhancing sectors, the productivity-enhancing agencies that promote people's incomes, people's livelihoods, and employments.

segments.speaker: Social Watch Philippines Co-convenor Dr. Maria Victoria Raquiza
segments.text: This tilts the budget towards fiscal obligations, infrastructure, defense, and law and order, and these are prioritized over enhancing productivity and increasing incomes for our people.

segments.speaker: Social Watch Philippines Co-convenor Dr. Maria Victoria Raquiza
Social Watch Philippines Co-convenor Dr. Maria Victoria Raquiza
segments.text: We are very, very disturbed by the lack of prioritization.

segments.speaker: Social Watch Philippines Co-convenor Dr. Maria Victoria Raquiza
segments.text: We are very, very disturbed by the lack of prioritization of productivity-enhancing economic activities which our people badly need, particularly in agriculture and MSMEs.

segments.speaker: Social Watch Philippines Co-convenor Dr. Maria Victoria Raquiza
segments.text: Second, so basically this imbalance raises a fundamental question.

segments.speaker: Social Watch Philippines Co-convenor Dr. Maria Victoria Raquiza
segments.text: How can we aspire to inclusive development without adequately investing in the productive capacities that enable Filipinos to secure decent work and lift themselves outside of poverty?

segments.speaker: Social Watch Philippines Co-convenor Dr. Maria Victoria Raquiza
Social Watch Philippines Co-convenor Dr. Maria Victoria Raquiza
segments.text: If we talk systemic, this is systemic.

segments.speaker: Social Watch Philippines Co-convenor Dr. Maria Victoria Raquiza
segments.text: Second, now we'll talk about human development.

segments.speaker: Social Watch Philippines Co-convenor Dr. Maria Victoria Raquiza
segments.text: The relegation of people's well-being, dignity, and human development has also been relegated to a secondary concern.

segments.speaker: Social Watch Philippines Co-convenor Dr. Maria Victoria Raquiza
segments.text: Infrastructure and debt service received the highest budgetary increases, while significant budget cuts have yet again been made to health, education, housing, and other essential social needs.

segments.speaker: Social Watch Philippines Co-convenor Dr. Maria Victoria Raquiza
segments.text: Now, this raises budgetary issues about the kinds of priorities of our policymakers.

segments.speaker: Social Watch Philippines Co-convenor Dr. Maria Victoria Raquiza
segments.text: I'm sorry to say, are we building the foundations for lasting human development, or are we merely managing the consequences of persistent poverty and inequality?

segments.speaker: Social Watch Philippines Co-convenor Dr. Maria Victoria Raquiza
segments.text: This is very residual social policy rather than transformative.

segments.speaker: Social Watch Philippines Co-convenor Dr. Maria Victoria Raquiza
segments.text: Third, and perhaps most troubling, is the persistence.

segments.speaker: Social Watch Philippines Co-convenor Dr. Maria Victoria Raquiza
segments.text: This is the result of appropriations vulnerable to pork barrel and patronage politics, which our colleagues in People's Budget Coalition have already very much focused on.

segments.speaker: Social Watch Philippines Co-convenor Dr. Maria Victoria Raquiza
segments.text: Our analysis identifies ₱221 billion of DPWH's BIP program in the House-approved budget, ₱72 billion above the proposed NEP allocation.

segments.speaker: Social Watch Philippines Co-convenor Dr. Maria Victoria Raquiza
segments.text: These practices are especially troubling in light of the Supreme Court's recent ruling.

segments.speaker: Social Watch Philippines Co-convenor Dr. Maria Victoria Raquiza
segments.text: This problem of political discretion, now we go to soft pork, extends to social protection programs, which are indispensable in a country marked by widespread poverty and inequality.

segments.speaker: Social Watch Philippines Co-convenor Dr. Maria Victoria Raquiza
segments.text: The House-approved GAB also contains what may be characterized as soft pork, and our colleagues in PBC have mentioned this in a very thorough way.

segments.speaker: Social Watch Philippines Co-convenor Dr. Maria Victoria Raquiza
segments.text: At the very least, we urge the Senate to restore their allocations.

segments.speaker: Social Watch Philippines Co-convenor Dr. Maria Victoria Raquiza
segments.text: to the NEP level, and the freed-up resources go to [unclear]. I will talk about that later in the recommendations.

segments.speaker: Social Watch Philippines Co-convenor Dr. Maria Victoria Raquiza
segments.text: But let us be clear, the problem is not social protection itself, but its appropriation for political ends.

segments.speaker: Social Watch Philippines Co-convenor Dr. Maria Victoria Raquiza
segments.text: So consider PhilHealth and MAIFIP, and my colleagues will talk about this much more extensively.

segments.speaker: Social Watch Philippines Co-convenor Dr. Maria Victoria Raquiza
segments.text: May pakalakang papel naman ang MAIFIP bilang safety net para sa mga pasyenteng kulang ang health coverage.

segments.speaker: Social Watch Philippines Co-convenor Dr. Maria Victoria Raquiza
segments.text: Ngunit meron na tayong PhilHealth eh.

segments.speaker: Social Watch Philippines Co-convenor Dr. Maria Victoria Raquiza
segments.text: Sa ilalim ng Universal Health Care Act, hindi dapat maging permanenteng kapalit ng PhilHealth sa isang parallel system ng medical assistance.

segments.speaker: Social Watch Philippines Co-convenor Dr. Maria Victoria Raquiza
segments.text: Kung kulang ang benepisyon ng PhilHealth sa tamang tugon, ito kasi ng PhilHealth.

segments.speaker: Social Watch Philippines Co-convenor Dr. Maria Victoria Raquiza
Social Watch Philippines Co-convenor Dr. Maria Victoria Raquiza
segments.text: Yet in the proposed 2027 budget, PhilHealth remains inadequately funded to fulfill its universal mandate.

segments.speaker: Social Watch Philippines Co-convenor Dr. Maria Victoria Raquiza
segments.text: While MAIFIP retains substantial allocations, which we all know is vulnerable to patronage politics.

segments.speaker: Social Watch Philippines Co-convenor Dr. Maria Victoria Raquiza
segments.text: Napakasakit ang isang Pilipino, hindi niya dapat itanong, sino ang malalipitan ko?

segments.speaker: Social Watch Philippines Co-convenor Dr. Maria Victoria Raquiza
segments.text: Ang dapat niyang sasabihin, covered ako, karapatan ko to.

segments.speaker: Social Watch Philippines Co-convenor Dr. Maria Victoria Raquiza
segments.text: Now to LGSF, which stands at 62.62 billion from the HGAB, as we know, is also a kind of pork barrel,

segments.speaker: Social Watch Philippines Co-convenor Dr. Maria Victoria Raquiza
segments.text: especially the FALBU, the SBDP, and the DRR Assistance Program.

segments.speaker: Social Watch Philippines Co-convenor Dr. Maria Victoria Raquiza
segments.text: These are all discretionary funds, no?

segments.speaker: Social Watch Philippines Co-convenor Dr. Maria Victoria Raquiza
segments.text: And are highly vulnerable to patronage politics.

segments.speaker: Social Watch Philippines Co-convenor Dr. Maria Victoria Raquiza
segments.text: And let's face it, especially as 2028 nears.

segments.speaker: Social Watch Philippines Co-convenor Dr. Maria Victoria Raquiza
segments.text: Adding soft pork, so if we add soft pork that I talked about earlier with the hard pork of BIP and LGSF,

segments.speaker: Social Watch Philippines Co-convenor Dr. Maria Victoria Raquiza
segments.text: we at least identified about 427 billion in appropriations that warrant rigorous scrutiny

segments.speaker: Social Watch Philippines Co-convenor Dr. Maria Victoria Raquiza
Social Watch Philippines Co-convenor Dr. Maria Victoria Raquiza
Social Watch Philippines Co-convenor Dr. Maria Victoria Raquiza
segments.text: So this brings us to a fundamental question.

segments.speaker: Social Watch Philippines Co-convenor Dr. Maria Victoria Raquiza
segments.text: Whose interest does our national budget ultimately serve?

segments.speaker: Social Watch Philippines Co-convenor Dr. Maria Victoria Raquiza
segments.text: The Filipino people or those who wield political power?

segments.speaker: Social Watch Philippines Co-convenor Dr. Maria Victoria Raquiza

segments.speaker: CitizenWatch Philippines Co-convenor Julia Kristine Basa
segments.text: Good afternoon, Honorable Chair Ejército, Senate President Katchilyan, and Vice Chair Senator Lawson.

segments.speaker: CitizenWatch Philippines Co-convenor Julia Kristine Basa
segments.text: We thank the Senate Committee on Finance for inviting civil society organizations to consult regarding the proposed 2027 budget.

segments.speaker: CitizenWatch Philippines Co-convenor Julia Kristine Basa
segments.text: As Congress continues to deliberate, Citizen Watch calls for greater consumer-centered public spending that prioritizes affordability, accessibility, and effective delivery of essential services.

segments.speaker: CitizenWatch Philippines Co-convenor Julia Kristine Basa
segments.text: We recognize the importance of adequate government funding for better public service.

segments.speaker: CitizenWatch Philippines Co-convenor Julia Kristine Basa
segments.text: However, we also emphasize that increased budget allocations must translate into tangible, measurable, and meaningful benefits for Filipino consumers.

segments.speaker: CitizenWatch Philippines Co-convenor Julia Kristine Basa
segments.text: Public spending must prioritize affordable and reliable electricity, accessible healthcare, safe and efficient public transportation, effective flood protection, improved digital services, and stronger consumer protection from the raging cost of living crisis.

segments.speaker: CitizenWatch Philippines Co-convenor Julia Kristine Basa
segments.text: We call on Congress and concerned government agencies to ensure that the proposed 2027 budget is implemented.

segments.speaker: CitizenWatch Philippines Co-convenor Julia Kristine Basa
segments.text: With transparency, accountability, efficient resource utilization, and strict monitoring of government projects and programs.

segments.speaker: CitizenWatch Philippines Co-convenor Julia Kristine Basa
segments.text: Investments must address the everyday needs of Filipino households, particularly low-income and vulnerable communities, while ensuring that public resources are not wasted through inefficiencies, delays, or questionable expenditures.

segments.speaker: CitizenWatch Philippines Co-convenor Julia Kristine Basa
segments.text: On healthcare, we welcome the proposed increase in the Cancer Assistance Fund.

segments.speaker: CitizenWatch Philippines Co-convenor Julia Kristine Basa
segments.text: And if approved, we urge the Department of Health to ensure that these additional resources are utilized efficiently and without delay to reach more patients and improve access to comprehensive cancer care.

segments.speaker: CitizenWatch Philippines Co-convenor Julia Kristine Basa
segments.text: Citizen Watch Philippines previously worked with Senator J.V. Ejercito as the principal author of the National Integrated Cancer Control Act.

segments.speaker: CitizenWatch Philippines Co-convenor Julia Kristine Basa
segments.text: At the same time, we emphasize the need to adequately fund our public education system.

segments.speaker: CitizenWatch Philippines Co-convenor Julia Kristine Basa
segments.text: As Education Secretary Angara has pointed out, funding gaps in the proposed 2027 budget could slow implementation of critical programs.

segments.speaker: CitizenWatch Philippines Co-convenor Julia Kristine Basa
segments.text: We therefore support efforts to restore and augment the funding for these essential programs.

segments.speaker: CitizenWatch Philippines Co-convenor Julia Kristine Basa
segments.text: Every peso of taxpayers' money must serve the public interest.

segments.speaker: CitizenWatch Philippines Co-convenor Julia Kristine Basa
segments.text: The true measure of the 2027 national budget should be whether Filipino families experiencing lower household expenses,

segments.speaker: CitizenWatch Philippines Co-convenor Julia Kristine Basa
segments.text: better access to essential services, greater protection from financial burdens, and meaningful improvements in their quality of life.

segments.speaker: CitizenWatch Philippines Co-convenor Julia Kristine Basa
segments.text: For Citizen Watch Philippines, a truly responsive national budget is one whose benefits are not only reflected in government reports and spending figures,

segments.speaker: CitizenWatch Philippines Co-convenor Julia Kristine Basa
segments.text: but are genuinely felt by ordinary Filipinos in their homes and in their communities.

segments.text: to fulfill the government's obligations under the Universal Health Care Act.

segments.speaker: Healthcare Professional Alliance Representative Dr. Albert Ong
segments.text: Since 2022, approximately P311 billion in earmarked revenues from Syntaxes, PCSO, and Pagcor

segments.speaker: Healthcare Professional Alliance Representative Dr. Albert Ong
segments.text: have been withheld or left unappropriated.

segments.speaker: Healthcare Professional Alliance Representative Dr. Albert Ong
segments.text: These resources were intended to help finance the UHC reforms

segments.speaker: Healthcare Professional Alliance Representative Dr. Albert Ong
segments.text: and should not be diverted, withheld, or left idle

segments.speaker: Healthcare Professional Alliance Representative Dr. Albert Ong
segments.text: when Filipinos continue to face catastrophic out-of-pocket health care costs.

segments.speaker: Healthcare Professional Alliance Representative Dr. Albert Ong
segments.text: The second provision that we have deep concern is the increase in the allocation for the MAIFIP

segments.speaker: Healthcare Professional Alliance Representative Dr. Albert Ong
segments.text: or the Medical Assistance for Indigent and Financially Incapacitated Patients

segments.speaker: Healthcare Professional Alliance Representative Dr. Albert Ong
segments.text: from approximately P24 billion to nearly P50 billion.

segments.speaker: Healthcare Professional Alliance Representative Dr. Albert Ong
segments.text: We understand that while financial assistance

segments.speaker: Healthcare Professional Alliance Representative Dr. Albert Ong
segments.text: to patients in need is essential,

segments.speaker: Healthcare Professional Alliance Representative Dr. Albert Ong
segments.text: the current system is fundamentally inequitable.

segments.speaker: Healthcare Professional Alliance Representative Dr. Albert Ong
segments.text: We observe, our members see that tens of thousands of Filipinos

segments.speaker: Healthcare Professional Alliance Representative Dr. Albert Ong
segments.text: are arbitrarily denied of MAIFIP benefits.

segments.speaker: Healthcare Professional Alliance Representative Dr. Albert Ong
segments.text: They come to us asking for help, yet we are often powerless

segments.speaker: Healthcare Professional Alliance Representative Dr. Albert Ong
segments.text: because of access to these funds depends on the discretion of our local officials.

segments.speaker: Healthcare Professional Alliance Representative Dr. Albert Ong
segments.text: Health care should not depend on whom a patient knows,

segments.speaker: Healthcare Professional Alliance Representative Dr. Albert Ong
segments.text: whom they can approach, or whom they can persuade to help them.

segments.speaker: Healthcare Professional Alliance Representative Dr. Albert Ong
segments.text: The amount of assistance a patient receives should be determined

segments.speaker: Healthcare Professional Alliance Representative Dr. Albert Ong
segments.text: by the nature and severity of their illness and the health care they require,

segments.speaker: Healthcare Professional Alliance Representative Dr. Albert Ong
Healthcare Professional Alliance Representative Dr. Albert Ong
segments.text: MAIFIP has consequently become vulnerable to use

segments.speaker: Healthcare Professional Alliance Representative Dr. Albert Ong
segments.text: as a political instrument and a mechanism of patronage.

segments.speaker: Healthcare Professional Alliance Representative Dr. Albert Ong
segments.text: Like what other resource persons mentioned here,

segments.speaker: Healthcare Professional Alliance Representative Dr. Albert Ong
segments.text: we advocate for the abolition of the discretionary,

segments.speaker: Healthcare Professional Alliance Representative Dr. Albert Ong
segments.text: medical assistance funds such as MAIFIP

segments.speaker: Healthcare Professional Alliance Representative Dr. Albert Ong
segments.text: and the transfer of these resources to PhilHealth,

segments.speaker: Healthcare Professional Alliance Representative Dr. Albert Ong
segments.text: where they can be administered through transparent,

segments.speaker: Healthcare Professional Alliance Representative Dr. Albert Ong
Healthcare Professional Alliance Representative Dr. Albert Ong
segments.text: that ensures assistance is determined by health care needs

segments.speaker: Healthcare Professional Alliance Representative Dr. Albert Ong
segments.text: and ability to pay, not political connections.

segments.speaker: Healthcare Professional Alliance Representative Dr. Albert Ong
segments.text: So ito po yung plea ng mga miyembro po ng HPAC.

segments.speaker: Healthcare Professional Alliance Representative Dr. Albert Ong
segments.text: Ito po yung apat na plea namin.

segments.speaker: Healthcare Professional Alliance Representative Dr. Albert Ong
segments.text: Una, immediate correction of the 2027 PhilHealth funding gap.

segments.speaker: Healthcare Professional Alliance Representative Dr. Albert Ong
segments.text: We urge the Congress and the...

segments.speaker: Healthcare Professional Alliance Representative Dr. Albert Ong
Healthcare Professional Alliance Representative Dr. Albert Ong
segments.text: to decisively close the approximately 170 billion funding shortfall

segments.speaker: Healthcare Professional Alliance Representative Dr. Albert Ong
segments.text: and provide PhilHealth with at least the full 244 billion

segments.speaker: Healthcare Professional Alliance Representative Dr. Albert Ong
Healthcare Professional Alliance Representative Dr. Albert Ong
segments.text: Second, full remittance and appropriation of PhilHealth funds.

segments.speaker: Healthcare Professional Alliance Representative Dr. Albert Ong
segments.text: We call for the immediate release and appropriation

segments.speaker: Healthcare Professional Alliance Representative Dr. Albert Ong
segments.text: of the cumulative 311 billion in PhilHealth,

segments.speaker: Healthcare Professional Alliance Representative Dr. Albert Ong
segments.text: unappropriated and unreleased syntax, pag-core, and PCS,

segments.speaker: Healthcare Professional Alliance Representative Dr. Albert Ong
Healthcare Professional Alliance Representative Dr. Albert Ong
Healthcare Professional Alliance Representative Dr. Albert Ong
segments.text: particularly to strengthen PhilHealth benefit packages

segments.speaker: Healthcare Professional Alliance Representative Dr. Albert Ong
segments.text: and reduce the burden of out-of-pocket spending.

segments.speaker: Healthcare Professional Alliance Representative Dr. Albert Ong
segments.text: Third, elimination of discretionary health patronage funds

segments.speaker: Healthcare Professional Alliance Representative Dr. Albert Ong
Healthcare Professional Alliance Representative Dr. Albert Ong
segments.text: We call for the transfer of discretionary medical assistance funds,

segments.speaker: Healthcare Professional Alliance Representative Dr. Albert Ong
Healthcare Professional Alliance Representative Dr. Albert Ong
segments.text: and their conversion into transparent, rules-based health benefits,

segments.speaker: Healthcare Professional Alliance Representative Dr. Albert Ong
Healthcare Professional Alliance Representative Dr. Albert Ong
segments.text: for indigent and financially incapacitated patients.

segments.speaker: Healthcare Professional Alliance Representative Dr. Albert Ong
Healthcare Professional Alliance Representative Dr. Albert Ong
segments.text: We demand full public disclosure and accountability

segments.speaker: Healthcare Professional Alliance Representative Dr. Albert Ong
segments.text: for all executive releases and congressional budget actions

segments.speaker: Healthcare Professional Alliance Representative Dr. Albert Ong
Healthcare Professional Alliance Representative Dr. Albert Ong
Healthcare Professional Alliance Representative Dr. Albert Ong
segments.text: and utilization of funds intended for PhilHealth

segments.speaker: Healthcare Professional Alliance Representative Dr. Albert Ong
Healthcare Professional Alliance Representative Dr. Albert Ong
segments.text: So every day, on the front lines of our healthcare system,

segments.speaker: Healthcare Professional Alliance Representative Dr. Albert Ong
segments.text: we witness the devastating human cost of these budget decisions.

segments.speaker: Healthcare Professional Alliance Representative Dr. Albert Ong
segments.text: As healthcare workers, we see the families of our patients

segments.speaker: Healthcare Professional Alliance Representative Dr. Albert Ong
segments.text: driven into deep poverty by catastrophic hospital bills.

segments.speaker: Healthcare Professional Alliance Representative Dr. Albert Ong
segments.text: We see patients delay or forego urgent treatment

segments.speaker: Healthcare Professional Alliance Representative Dr. Albert Ong
Healthcare Professional Alliance Representative Dr. Albert Ong
segments.text: We are forced to watch patients go without the funds

segments.speaker: Healthcare Professional Alliance Representative Dr. Albert Ong
segments.text: they need to receive the life-saving care.

segments.speaker: Healthcare Professional Alliance Representative Dr. Albert Ong
segments.text: And we see something that should never be acceptable

segments.speaker: Healthcare Professional Alliance Representative Dr. Albert Ong
Healthcare Professional Alliance Representative Dr. Albert Ong
segments.text: Filipinos are forced to beg, line up at politicians' offices,

segments.speaker: Healthcare Professional Alliance Representative Dr. Albert Ong
segments.text: and seek personal favor simply to obtain healthcare

segments.speaker: Healthcare Professional Alliance Representative Dr. Albert Ong
Healthcare Professional Alliance Representative Dr. Albert Ong
Healthcare Professional Alliance Representative Dr. Albert Ong
Healthcare Professional Alliance Representative Dr. Albert Ong
segments.text: And I'm sure all of us have the same sentiment

segments.speaker: Healthcare Professional Alliance Representative Dr. Albert Ong
Healthcare Professional Alliance Representative Dr. Albert Ong
segments.text: It must never be reduced to a discretionary fund

segments.speaker: Healthcare Professional Alliance Representative Dr. Albert Ong
Healthcare Professional Alliance Representative Dr. Albert Ong
segments.text: It must never be reduced to political patronage

segments.speaker: Healthcare Professional Alliance Representative Dr. Albert Ong
Healthcare Professional Alliance Representative Dr. Albert Ong
segments.text: So kami po, ang mga miyembro po ng Healthcare Professional Alliance,

segments.speaker: Healthcare Professional Alliance Representative Dr. Albert Ong
Healthcare Professional Alliance Representative Dr. Albert Ong
segments.text: we call on Congress, the Executive,

segments.speaker: Healthcare Professional Alliance Representative Dr. Albert Ong
segments.text: and all those interested with the people's resources

segments.speaker: Healthcare Professional Alliance Representative Dr. Albert Ong
segments.text: to put patients and people, not politics,

segments.speaker: Healthcare Professional Alliance Representative Dr. Albert Ong
segments.text: at the center of the 2027 National Budget.

segments.text: Next po is for DILG, NACC, and NCIP, a total combined amount of 3.6 million po which includes improved systems.

segments.speaker: World Vision Advocacy Specialist Pauline Navarro
segments.text: and protocols for OSAEM and SISAEC case identification, referral management, and monitoring.

segments.speaker: World Vision Advocacy Specialist Pauline Navarro
segments.text: So yung pag-train po ng mga LGUs on case management and referral system.

segments.speaker: World Vision Advocacy Specialist Pauline Navarro
segments.text: Users training on ASO for NACC and Maraco and capacity building po for IP communities including children po na makasama po sila sa capacity building on improved capacity.

segments.speaker: World Vision Advocacy Specialist Pauline Navarro
segments.text: Next po, ito po yung summary lang po nung aming mga proposals.

segments.speaker: World Vision Advocacy Specialist Pauline Navarro
segments.text: So ito po ay katuwang po ng mga agencies na kasama po namin sa NCC OSAEC-SISAEM and we've already shared this with them as well po.

segments.speaker: World Vision Advocacy Specialist Pauline Navarro
segments.text: Yung sa tingin po namin na dapat i-prioritize dahil po yung ating strategic plan ay until 2028 na lang po.

segments.speaker: World Vision Advocacy Specialist Pauline Navarro
segments.text: And we're hoping na by 2027 ay magkaroon po ng sapat na pono.

segments.speaker: World Vision Advocacy Specialist Pauline Navarro
segments.text: Para magawa po itong ating mga PPAs under the strategic plan.

segments.speaker: World Vision Advocacy Specialist Pauline Navarro
segments.text: So next po is yung, ito po meron po kaming 5 PPAs outside ng costed implementation plan na we think are also important po to include sa ating budget.

segments.speaker: World Vision Advocacy Specialist Pauline Navarro
segments.text: So beyond the costed implementation plan, we think that these are essential to address child protection and mental health needs.

segments.speaker: World Vision Advocacy Specialist Pauline Navarro
segments.text: Yung ilan po dito, I think na-mention na rin po kanina.

segments.speaker: World Vision Advocacy Specialist Pauline Navarro
segments.text: So i-re-reiterate ko na lang po siya.

segments.speaker: World Vision Advocacy Specialist Pauline Navarro
segments.text: So in child-friendly and accessible mental health support service amounting to 4 billion.

segments.speaker: World Vision Advocacy Specialist Pauline Navarro
segments.text: Kasama din po yung nabanggit ko na kanina na women and children protection units in 38 DOH-retained hospitals amounting to 145 million plus.

segments.speaker: World Vision Advocacy Specialist Pauline Navarro
segments.text: And then ito po ay budget restoration of the NCC against OSAEC-SISAEM.

segments.speaker: World Vision Advocacy Specialist Pauline Navarro
segments.text: And sinare din po sa amin ng sekretaryat na may sinentong letter dito.

segments.speaker: World Vision Advocacy Specialist Pauline Navarro
segments.text: May visa office po ninyo for the request to restore po yung kanila pong budget from 2026.

segments.speaker: World Vision Advocacy Specialist Pauline Navarro
World Vision Advocacy Specialist Pauline Navarro
segments.text: Of course, budget restoration and augmentation po ng child protection program sa DepEd naman po ito.

segments.speaker: World Vision Advocacy Specialist Pauline Navarro
segments.text: Na maibalik po yung budget line item na child protection program.

segments.speaker: World Vision Advocacy Specialist Pauline Navarro
segments.text: Kasi po sa ngayon ay nasubsume na po siya sa learner support program nila.

segments.speaker: World Vision Advocacy Specialist Pauline Navarro
segments.text: And ang amount po din is 44 million.

segments.speaker: World Vision Advocacy Specialist Pauline Navarro
segments.text: Ito din po wish list ng 68 additional plantelia positions for the NCC-OSAEC-SISAEM sekretaryat amounting to 41 million pesos.

segments.speaker: World Vision Advocacy Specialist Pauline Navarro
segments.text: So ayan po yung summary po yung kabuuan po nung aming pong request na 4.4 billion pesos po.

segments.speaker: World Vision Advocacy Specialist Pauline Navarro
segments.text: So I'd like to end my presentation po by saying po again na ang bata ang bida sa budget at pera ng taong bayan ay dapat para sa taong bayan.

segments.speaker: World Vision Advocacy Specialist Pauline Navarro
segments.text: So sana po maisip niyo na ito ay wish list.

segments.speaker: World Vision Advocacy Specialist Pauline Navarro
segments.text: Hindi lamang ng mga nakakatanda pero ng mga bata din po lalo na po ngayong Pasko.

segments.speaker: World Vision Advocacy Specialist Pauline Navarro
Senator Joseph Victor "JV" G. Ejercito
Senator Joseph Victor "JV" G. Ejercito
segments.text: Next is sa Unang Hakbang Foundation.

segments.speaker: Senator Joseph Victor "JV" G. Ejercito
Unang Hakbang Foundation Program Manager Mary Aieen Padoga
Senator Joseph Victor "JV" G. Ejercito
Unang Hakbang Foundation Program Manager Mary Aieen Padoga
Unang Hakbang Foundation Program Manager Mary Aieen Padoga
Unang Hakbang Foundation Program Manager Mary Aieen Padoga
segments.text: Good afternoon po honorable senators who are here as well as all the CSOs po nandito.

segments.speaker: Unang Hakbang Foundation Program Manager Mary Aieen Padoga
segments.text: So Unang Hakbang is an operating foundation that provides remedial classes in reading math.

segments.speaker: Unang Hakbang Foundation Program Manager Mary Aieen Padoga
segments.text: For children at risk of dropping out of school, living in the poorest or poorer sections of Mandaluyong and Pampanga.

segments.speaker: Unang Hakbang Foundation Program Manager Mary Aieen Padoga
segments.text: Issues that confront us daily and which impact how children learn are hunger, malnourished, lack of water and proper sanitation and inability of parents to support their children's learning.

segments.speaker: Unang Hakbang Foundation Program Manager Mary Aieen Padoga
segments.text: These same issues are among those that have limited country's progress on the 2030 Sustainable Development Goals.

segments.speaker: Unang Hakbang Foundation Program Manager Mary Aieen Padoga
segments.text: So ang sa Unang Hakbang lang po ay magbibigay lang po kami ng tatlong recommendations for this session.

segments.speaker: Unang Hakbang Foundation Program Manager Mary Aieen Padoga
segments.text: So yung una po ay yung hunger and malnutrition.

segments.speaker: Unang Hakbang Foundation Program Manager Mary Aieen Padoga
segments.text: So we recommend na sana po ay may restoration of 26 budget of dev ed for school based feeding program.

segments.speaker: Unang Hakbang Foundation Program Manager Mary Aieen Padoga
Unang Hakbang Foundation Program Manager Mary Aieen Padoga
Unang Hakbang Foundation Program Manager Mary Aieen Padoga
segments.text: Yung pangalawa naman po ay yung provision of 300 million in DA budget for the research and initial implementation of a nutrition sensitive agricultural program and an agricultural supply chain network centered on bringing produce to areas near families and schools.

segments.speaker: Unang Hakbang Foundation Program Manager Mary Aieen Padoga
segments.text: Yung pangalawang issue naman po ay yung bullying and learners mental health.

segments.speaker: Unang Hakbang Foundation Program Manager Mary Aieen Padoga
Unang Hakbang Foundation Program Manager Mary Aieen Padoga
segments.text: Hindi lang po talaga kumbaga pabata ng pabata ang may issue or usapin na patungkol sa mental health.

segments.speaker: Unang Hakbang Foundation Program Manager Mary Aieen Padoga
segments.text: So hindi ko na i-explain why kasi it's really issues that we are really encounter right now.

segments.speaker: Unang Hakbang Foundation Program Manager Mary Aieen Padoga
segments.text: So yung recommendation lang po namin is the provision of 300 million for learners welfare intended to strengthen child protection.

segments.speaker: Unang Hakbang Foundation Program Manager Mary Aieen Padoga
segments.text: And the training of all teachers and students to recognize peers who might need help.

segments.speaker: Unang Hakbang Foundation Program Manager Mary Aieen Padoga
segments.text: The aim is to initially address the need of the 10,000 that EDCOM 2 has identified as lacking even an anti-bullying policy.

segments.speaker: Unang Hakbang Foundation Program Manager Mary Aieen Padoga
segments.text: And another one is the provision of another 300 million to support inset training on a positive parenting in schools to create a more just in a peaceful environment in campuses.

segments.speaker: Unang Hakbang Foundation Program Manager Mary Aieen Padoga
segments.text: And another issues naman po ay yun nga hindi din matutulungan ang mga bata kung hindi din natin i-train or hindi tayo sama-sama para magkaroon ng peaceful environment ang mga bata sa Pilipinas.

segments.speaker: Unang Hakbang Foundation Program Manager Mary Aieen Padoga
segments.text: So ito naman po ay nag-focus sa SDG 4, SDG 5, and SDG 16 ay ang yung adult education and lifelong learning.

segments.speaker: Unang Hakbang Foundation Program Manager Mary Aieen Padoga
segments.text: So ito it's all in its house EST or education and skill training.

segments.speaker: Unang Hakbang Foundation Program Manager Mary Aieen Padoga
segments.text: And for implementers, DepEd reporting that 2017, there were at least 19 million adults or 18 to 59 years old, comprising a third of that age group who had not completed their basic education.

segments.speaker: Unang Hakbang Foundation Program Manager Mary Aieen Padoga
segments.text: In the quality basic education development plan, on DepEd underscored that need the strong collaboration involving all education stakeholders from national institutions.

segments.speaker: Unang Hakbang Foundation Program Manager Mary Aieen Padoga
segments.text: From public to central, public to private, and most notably teachers, parents, and children.

segments.speaker: Unang Hakbang Foundation Program Manager Mary Aieen Padoga
segments.text: The entire nation must work together to deliver better quality basic education for all and contribute to inclusive economic growth in the Philippines.

segments.speaker: Unang Hakbang Foundation Program Manager Mary Aieen Padoga
segments.text: So through that, our recommendation is the restoration of the line item for community learning centers to house alts and lifelong learning classes.

segments.speaker: Unang Hakbang Foundation Program Manager Mary Aieen Padoga
Unang Hakbang Foundation Program Manager Mary Aieen Padoga
segments.text: For the construction of CLCs, 200 million until all municipalities have at least one CLC.

segments.speaker: Unang Hakbang Foundation Program Manager Mary Aieen Padoga
segments.text: Specified that local government support fund or LGSF may be also used to finance the construction of CLCs and the training of women as para-counselors to support effort to eliminate bullying and improve the mental health of students.

segments.speaker: Unang Hakbang Foundation Program Manager Mary Aieen Padoga
segments.text: And 100 million honoraria for volunteers who teach in CLCs.

segments.speaker: Unang Hakbang Foundation Program Manager Mary Aieen Padoga
segments.text: And the CLCs also take notice not just for learning, this is also a safe space for children, for youth, and even for the parents.

segments.speaker: Unang Hakbang Foundation Program Manager Mary Aieen Padoga
segments.text: So I think that's all po. Thank you.

segments.speaker: Senator Joseph Victor "JV" G. Ejercito
Senator Joseph Victor "JV" G. Ejercito
Senator Joseph Victor "JV" G. Ejercito
E-Net Philippines National Executive Board Member Prof. Flora C. Arellano
segments.text: Sen. J.B. Ejercito, Chairperson of the Senate Committee on Finance.

segments.speaker: E-Net Philippines National Executive Board Member Prof. Flora C. Arellano
segments.text: Sen. Fanpilo Lacson, Co-Chair ng Finance Committee.

segments.speaker: E-Net Philippines National Executive Board Member Prof. Flora C. Arellano
segments.text: At ang ating Senate President, Wyn Gatchalian.

segments.speaker: E-Net Philippines National Executive Board Member Prof. Flora C. Arellano
segments.text: At mga kasama sa Civil Society Organizations.

segments.speaker: E-Net Philippines National Executive Board Member Prof. Flora C. Arellano
segments.text: At maging ang aking kasama rin sa INET Philippines.

segments.speaker: E-Net Philippines National Executive Board Member Prof. Flora C. Arellano
segments.text: Na walang iba, kundi ang aming Advocacy Officer, Mercy Chan.

segments.speaker: E-Net Philippines National Executive Board Member Prof. Flora C. Arellano
segments.text: Magandang hapon po sa inyong lahat.

segments.speaker: E-Net Philippines National Executive Board Member Prof. Flora C. Arellano
E-Net Philippines National Executive Board Member Prof. Flora C. Arellano
segments.text: Ang Education Network for INET Philippines.

segments.speaker: E-Net Philippines National Executive Board Member Prof. Flora C. Arellano
segments.text: Isang pambansang koalisyon na binubuo po ng 100 organizations.

segments.speaker: E-Net Philippines National Executive Board Member Prof. Flora C. Arellano
E-Net Philippines National Executive Board Member Prof. Flora C. Arellano
segments.text: Advocating for inclusive, equitable, quality education for all.

segments.speaker: E-Net Philippines National Executive Board Member Prof. Flora C. Arellano
segments.text: At siya po ang lead organizations education cluster ng Alternative Budget Initiative under Social Watch Philippines.

segments.speaker: E-Net Philippines National Executive Board Member Prof. Flora C. Arellano
segments.text: At nagpapasalamat po kami sa Senado for this opportunity to present our recommendations on the House-approved FY2027 General Appropriations Bill.

segments.speaker: E-Net Philippines National Executive Board Member Prof. Flora C. Arellano
E-Net Philippines National Executive Board Member Prof. Flora C. Arellano
segments.text: education cannot be declared a national priority while essential programs remain unfunded.

segments.speaker: E-Net Philippines National Executive Board Member Prof. Flora C. Arellano
segments.text: Legal mandates lack adequate resources and marginalized learners continue to be left behind.

segments.speaker: E-Net Philippines National Executive Board Member Prof. Flora C. Arellano
segments.text: While the House government maintains a substantial allocation for education,

segments.speaker: E-Net Philippines National Executive Board Member Prof. Flora C. Arellano
segments.text: what matters is not only how much government spends,

segments.speaker: E-Net Philippines National Executive Board Member Prof. Flora C. Arellano
segments.text: but where resources go, who benefit,

segments.speaker: E-Net Philippines National Executive Board Member Prof. Flora C. Arellano
segments.text: and whether the budget addresses persistent inequalities in education.

segments.speaker: E-Net Philippines National Executive Board Member Prof. Flora C. Arellano
segments.text: Based on our review of the House GAAP and INET's Alternative Budget Proposal,

segments.speaker: E-Net Philippines National Executive Board Member Prof. Flora C. Arellano
segments.text: we urge the Senate to address four priorities.

segments.speaker: E-Net Philippines National Executive Board Member Prof. Flora C. Arellano
segments.text: First, restore and expand funding for inclusive education and lifelong learning.

segments.speaker: E-Net Philippines National Executive Board Member Prof. Flora C. Arellano
segments.text: Ang krisis edukasyon na hindi lamang tumutukoy.

segments.speaker: E-Net Philippines National Executive Board Member Prof. Flora C. Arellano
segments.text: Sa mga batang nasa loob ng paaralan,

segments.speaker: E-Net Philippines National Executive Board Member Prof. Flora C. Arellano
segments.text: kundi sa mahigit na sampung milyon na mga bata at kabataan na wala sa paaralan.

segments.speaker: E-Net Philippines National Executive Board Member Prof. Flora C. Arellano
segments.text: At gayon din, mahigit sa labing siyam na milyon adults who missed out of education.

segments.speaker: E-Net Philippines National Executive Board Member Prof. Flora C. Arellano
segments.text: Ang panawagan pong ito namin, natin, dapat po'y walang naiiwan.

segments.speaker: E-Net Philippines National Executive Board Member Prof. Flora C. Arellano
E-Net Philippines National Executive Board Member Prof. Flora C. Arellano
segments.text: We acknowledge the House increases for special needs education in SNED,

segments.speaker: E-Net Philippines National Executive Board Member Prof. Flora C. Arellano
segments.text: indigenous people education, and madrasa education.

segments.speaker: E-Net Philippines National Executive Board Member Prof. Flora C. Arellano
segments.text: However, these allocations remain below their FY2026 levels and fall short of what is needed.

segments.speaker: E-Net Philippines National Executive Board Member Prof. Flora C. Arellano
segments.text: INET proposes P2.393 billion for SNED.

segments.speaker: E-Net Philippines National Executive Board Member Prof. Flora C. Arellano
segments.text: Kung titignan po natin, noong 2026, it's P1.040.

segments.speaker: E-Net Philippines National Executive Board Member Prof. Flora C. Arellano
segments.text: P2.393 billion na bawasan to support schools, operationalize inclusive learning resource centers,

segments.speaker: E-Net Philippines National Executive Board Member Prof. Flora C. Arellano
segments.text: strengthen child find, and provide accessible learning materials and support services.

segments.speaker: E-Net Philippines National Executive Board Member Prof. Flora C. Arellano
segments.text: For the alternative learning system and lifelong learning,

segments.speaker: E-Net Philippines National Executive Board Member Prof. Flora C. Arellano
segments.text: the House GAAP retains P3.849 billion under the broader Flexible Learning Options Program.

segments.speaker: E-Net Philippines National Executive Board Member Prof. Flora C. Arellano
E-Net Philippines National Executive Board Member Prof. Flora C. Arellano
E-Net Philippines National Executive Board Member Prof. Flora C. Arellano
segments.text: E-Net proposes P5.55 billion to expand ALS access,

segments.speaker: E-Net Philippines National Executive Board Member Prof. Flora C. Arellano
E-Net Philippines National Executive Board Member Prof. Flora C. Arellano
segments.text: for working adults and community learning centers,

segments.speaker: E-Net Philippines National Executive Board Member Prof. Flora C. Arellano
E-Net Philippines National Executive Board Member Prof. Flora C. Arellano
segments.text: We call for P5 billion in dedicated funding for last mile and GHIDA schools

segments.speaker: E-Net Philippines National Executive Board Member Prof. Flora C. Arellano
segments.text: and adequate support for indigenous and Madrasa education.

segments.speaker: E-Net Philippines National Executive Board Member Prof. Flora C. Arellano
E-Net Philippines National Executive Board Member Prof. Flora C. Arellano
E-Net Philippines National Executive Board Member Prof. Flora C. Arellano
segments.text: protect, and effectively implement funding for the ARAL program

segments.speaker: E-Net Philippines National Executive Board Member Prof. Flora C. Arellano
segments.text: and appropriations must translate into actual tutoring and learning recovery

segments.speaker: E-Net Philippines National Executive Board Member Prof. Flora C. Arellano
segments.text: for struggling learners with funded tutors,

segments.speaker: E-Net Philippines National Executive Board Member Prof. Flora C. Arellano
E-Net Philippines National Executive Board Member Prof. Flora C. Arellano
segments.text: and transparent reporting on delivery and results.

segments.speaker: E-Net Philippines National Executive Board Member Prof. Flora C. Arellano
E-Net Philippines National Executive Board Member Prof. Flora C. Arellano
segments.text: restore and strengthen program-supporting learners' nutrition,

segments.speaker: E-Net Philippines National Executive Board Member Prof. Flora C. Arellano
E-Net Philippines National Executive Board Member Prof. Flora C. Arellano
segments.text: The House GAAP retains 11.431 billion for the screening program,

segments.speaker: E-Net Philippines National Executive Board Member Prof. Flora C. Arellano
segments.text: substantially below the 25.695 billion allocation in FY2026.

segments.speaker: E-Net Philippines National Executive Board Member Prof. Flora C. Arellano
segments.text: ENET proposes 42.295 billion to restore existing funding,

segments.speaker: E-Net Philippines National Executive Board Member Prof. Flora C. Arellano
segments.text: expand feeding to 2 million additional learners,

segments.speaker: E-Net Philippines National Executive Board Member Prof. Flora C. Arellano
E-Net Philippines National Executive Board Member Prof. Flora C. Arellano
segments.text: And then, we call for dedicated funding for comprehensive school safety,

segments.speaker: E-Net Philippines National Executive Board Member Prof. Flora C. Arellano
segments.text: child protection, school mental health, and education in emergencies.

segments.speaker: E-Net Philippines National Executive Board Member Prof. Flora C. Arellano
segments.text: Beyond physical security, schools need prevention and response system for bullying, violence, abuse, discrimination, and disasters,

segments.speaker: E-Net Philippines National Executive Board Member Prof. Flora C. Arellano
segments.text: accessible reporting and referral mechanisms, trained personnel, and psychosocial support.

segments.speaker: E-Net Philippines National Executive Board Member Prof. Flora C. Arellano
segments.text: Funding must support a whole school, inclusive and rights-based approach, not merely new mandates without implementation resources.

segments.speaker: E-Net Philippines National Executive Board Member Prof. Flora C. Arellano
segments.text: Third, adequately fund teachers' welfare, school personnel, and inclusive teaching.

segments.speaker: E-Net Philippines National Executive Board Member Prof. Flora C. Arellano
segments.text: We urge the Senate to address continuing shortages of teachers, school principals, and administrative personnel.

segments.speaker: E-Net Philippines National Executive Board Member Prof. Flora C. Arellano
segments.text: ENET proposes funding for 14,274 additional teaching positions, additional principals, and administrative officers,

segments.speaker: E-Net Philippines National Executive Board Member Prof. Flora C. Arellano
segments.text: and 4.8 million for teaching overload compensation.

segments.speaker: E-Net Philippines National Executive Board Member Prof. Flora C. Arellano
segments.text: We also call for full funding of the Magna Carta benefits, including special hardship allowances,

segments.speaker: E-Net Philippines National Executive Board Member Prof. Flora C. Arellano
segments.text: transfer and deployment support, and teachers' mental health services.

segments.speaker: E-Net Philippines National Executive Board Member Prof. Flora C. Arellano
segments.text: Actually, RA 4670 is still in problem.

segments.speaker: E-Net Philippines National Executive Board Member Prof. Flora C. Arellano
segments.text: The correct implementation and full implementation of the Magna Carta.

segments.speaker: E-Net Philippines National Executive Board Member Prof. Flora C. Arellano
E-Net Philippines National Executive Board Member Prof. Flora C. Arellano
segments.text: No, we would like to ask your support for this.

segments.speaker: E-Net Philippines National Executive Board Member Prof. Flora C. Arellano
segments.text: Further, we propose 340 million for positive discipline in everyday teaching with disability inclusion perspective.

segments.speaker: E-Net Philippines National Executive Board Member Prof. Flora C. Arellano
segments.text: Training for 100,000 teachers initially to strengthen positive discipline and inclusive disability responsive teaching.

segments.speaker: E-Net Philippines National Executive Board Member Prof. Flora C. Arellano
segments.text: Quality education requires teachers whose rights are respected, well-protected, and professionalized.

segments.speaker: E-Net Philippines National Executive Board Member Prof. Flora C. Arellano
E-Net Philippines National Executive Board Member Prof. Flora C. Arellano
segments.text: Fourth, strengthen financing for early childhood education and underserved regions, particularly BARM.

segments.speaker: E-Net Philippines National Executive Board Member Prof. Flora C. Arellano
segments.text: We call for adequate investments in supplementary feeding, child development centers,

segments.speaker: E-Net Philippines National Executive Board Member Prof. Flora C. Arellano
segments.text: and professionalization and fair compensation of child development workers and teachers.

segments.speaker: E-Net Philippines National Executive Board Member Prof. Flora C. Arellano
segments.text: For BARM, we propose targeted investments in ALS community learning centers,

segments.speaker: E-Net Philippines National Executive Board Member Prof. Flora C. Arellano
E-Net Philippines National Executive Board Member Prof. Flora C. Arellano
segments.text: and learning recovery with resources directed to the most disadvantaged and conflict-affected communities.

segments.speaker: E-Net Philippines National Executive Board Member Prof. Flora C. Arellano
segments.text: Finally, we urge the Senate to ensure transparency, accountability, and equity in budget realignments.

segments.speaker: E-Net Philippines National Executive Board Member Prof. Flora C. Arellano
segments.text: Low fund utilization should not automatically be equated with low demand or divinish need.

segments.speaker: E-Net Philippines National Executive Board Member Prof. Flora C. Arellano
segments.text: It may reflect procurement delays, inadequate institutional capacity, and implementation bottlenecks

segments.speaker: E-Net Philippines National Executive Board Member Prof. Flora C. Arellano
E-Net Philippines National Executive Board Member Prof. Flora C. Arellano
segments.text: The government must address, not use as justification for reducing essential education allocations.

segments.speaker: E-Net Philippines National Executive Board Member Prof. Flora C. Arellano
segments.text: We therefore urge the Senate to scrutinize house budget realignments,

segments.speaker: E-Net Philippines National Executive Board Member Prof. Flora C. Arellano
segments.text: ensure clear program-level allocations, and protect resources for marginalized learners.

segments.speaker: E-Net Philippines National Executive Board Member Prof. Flora C. Arellano
E-Net Philippines National Executive Board Member Prof. Flora C. Arellano
segments.text: INET Philippines calls on the Senate

segments.speaker: E-Net Philippines National Executive Board Member Prof. Flora C. Arellano
segments.text: 1. to restore cuts to essential education programs,

segments.speaker: E-Net Philippines National Executive Board Member Prof. Flora C. Arellano
segments.text: expand investments or address persistent education inequalities,

segments.speaker: E-Net Philippines National Executive Board Member Prof. Flora C. Arellano
E-Net Philippines National Executive Board Member Prof. Flora C. Arellano
segments.text: Kung kailan marami tayong mga batas na naipasa, bumaba ang budget.

segments.speaker: E-Net Philippines National Executive Board Member Prof. Flora C. Arellano
segments.text: Halimbawa lang po ng mga mandates natin.

segments.speaker: E-Net Philippines National Executive Board Member Prof. Flora C. Arellano
E-Net Philippines National Executive Board Member Prof. Flora C. Arellano
E-Net Philippines National Executive Board Member Prof. Flora C. Arellano
E-Net Philippines National Executive Board Member Prof. Flora C. Arellano
segments.text: And then, 12321, Last Mile Schools Act.

segments.speaker: E-Net Philippines National Executive Board Member Prof. Flora C. Arellano
segments.text: And RA 4670, Magna Karta for Public School Teachers.

segments.speaker: E-Net Philippines National Executive Board Member Prof. Flora C. Arellano
segments.text: Protect education equity by prioritizing learners and communities facing the greatest barriers.

segments.speaker: E-Net Philippines National Executive Board Member Prof. Flora C. Arellano
segments.text: We respectfully submit our detailed alternative budget proposals for consideration in the Senate's amendment to the FY2027 GAP.

segments.speaker: E-Net Philippines National Executive Board Member Prof. Flora C. Arellano
segments.text: The challenge is not simply to maintain a large education budget,

segments.speaker: E-Net Philippines National Executive Board Member Prof. Flora C. Arellano
segments.text: but to ensure that every peso advances the right to inclusive, equitable, and quality education for all,

segments.speaker: E-Net Philippines National Executive Board Member Prof. Flora C. Arellano
segments.text: especially those who have been historically underserved and left behind.

segments.speaker: E-Net Philippines National Executive Board Member Prof. Flora C. Arellano
segments.text: Kaya nga po, pondo para sa karapatan ng mga mag-aaral sa edukasyon at edukasyon para sa lahat.

segments.speaker: E-Net Philippines National Executive Board Member Prof. Flora C. Arellano
segments.text: Mula sa INET Philippines, Education Network Flora Arillano,

segments.speaker: E-Net Philippines National Executive Board Member Prof. Flora C. Arellano
E-Net Philippines National Executive Board Member Prof. Flora C. Arellano
Senator Joseph Victor "JV" G. Ejercito
segments.text: Maraming salamat po, Professor Flora Arillano.

segments.speaker: Senator Joseph Victor "JV" G. Ejercito
segments.text: Next is Mr. Humphrey Soriano from Center for Youth Advocacy.

segments.speaker: Multiply-Ed Representative Humphrey Soriano
segments.text: Good afternoon, Mr. Chairperson and Honorable Members of the Committee.

segments.text: Magkano po ba ang ginagastos ng ating pamahalaan sa mga may kapansanan?

segments.speaker: Filipino Sign Language National Network Convenor Dr. Liza B. Martinez
segments.text: Isa sa mga pinakamahalagang aming nadiskubre at hindi namin alam kung tama ito o meron ng kasunod na ibang aralin,

segments.speaker: Filipino Sign Language National Network Convenor Dr. Liza B. Martinez

segments.speaker: Filipino Sign Language National Network Convenor Dr. Liza B. Martinez
segments.text: Sa susunod na slide, mapapakita namin ayon sa aming pagsusuri,

segments.text: Ilang bang Pilipino ang may mga may kapansanan?

segments.speaker: Filipino Sign Language National Network Convenor Dr. Liza B. Martinez

segments.speaker: Filipino Sign Language National Network Convenor Dr. Liza B. Martinez

segments.speaker: Filipino Sign Language National Network Convenor Dr. Liza B. Martinez
segments.text: Sa ngayon, tinatayang 12.9 million Pilipinos with disabilities ang nasa Pilipinas.

segments.speaker: Filipino Sign Language National Network Convenor Dr. Liza B. Martinez
segments.text: Subalit kung titignan natin ang bilang na ito,

segments.speaker: Filipino Sign Language National Network Convenor Dr. Liza B. Martinez
segments.text: ang 12.9 million na may kapansanan kailangan doblehin

segments.speaker: Filipino Sign Language National Network Convenor Dr. Liza B. Martinez
segments.text: kasi kailangang may isang miyembro ng pamamahay na kailangan magbantay o mag-alaga

segments.speaker: Filipino Sign Language National Network Convenor Dr. Liza B. Martinez
segments.text: at ikinalulukot namin usually ito ay babae, usually ito ay ang ina.

segments.speaker: Filipino Sign Language National Network Convenor Dr. Liza B. Martinez
segments.text: Kailangan din natin triplehin kasi pag merong may isang may kapansanan

Filipino Sign Language National Network Convenor Dr. Liza B. Martinez
segments.text: kailangan pang liban dun sa ina na hindi na makakapagtrabaho,

segments.speaker: Filipino Sign Language National Network Convenor Dr. Liza B. Martinez
segments.text: makakapaghanap buhay o makakagawa ng iba pa.

segments.speaker: Filipino Sign Language National Network Convenor Dr. Liza B. Martinez
segments.text: ay meron pang isang kailangang sumalo sa dagdag na gastos ng pamamahay dahil sa kapansanan.

segments.speaker: Filipino Sign Language National Network Convenor Dr. Liza B. Martinez
segments.text: So effectively, 12.9 million Filipinos with disabilities is equivalent to 36 million

segments.speaker: Filipino Sign Language National Network Convenor Dr. Liza B. Martinez
segments.text: or one-third of the entire Philippine population impacted by disability, directly or indirectly.

segments.speaker: Filipino Sign Language National Network Convenor Dr. Liza B. Martinez
segments.text: What to do? Ito po ang hinihiling namin. Di kami humihingi ng appropriations.

segments.text: Ang kailangan namin ay ang pagsik ng Senado kasi talagang bigong-bigo kami sa Kongreso.

segments.text: Sa dami ng iba't ibang NGAs na kailangan magpatupad ng laging sinasabing inclusive kami,

segments.text: It's only 0.12% of this year's GAAM.

segments.text: Karamihan po hindi nakakaalam na dito po sa 1.76 billion, kukunin din sana ang pondo para sa iba pang busway sa C5, sa Quezon Avenue at sa Ortigas Avenue.

segments.speaker: Move As One Coalition Representative Ysabel Eugene G. Agregado
segments.text: Ito pong 75 million, ang mapapondohan lang po nito ay malamang po ay janitorial and security personnel.

segments.speaker: Move As One Coalition Representative Ysabel Eugene G. Agregado
segments.text: Ganon din po ang nangyari sa Cebu BRT, 4% lang din po ng original DOTR proposal ang napondohan at ito po ay makakaapekto sa sobrang dami pong commuters na nasa Cebu.

segments.speaker: Move As One Coalition Representative Ysabel Eugene G. Agregado
segments.text: Si Sen. JV kakagaling lang din po sa Cebu checking on the health facility so I'm sure he knows about this then.

segments.speaker: Move As One Coalition Representative Ysabel Eugene G. Agregado
segments.text: Ito po, ang nag-trending ngayon at nagvaviral for good reason ang experience po ng mga commuters sa LRT2.

segments.text: 12.8 billion to purchase additional trainsets for the LRT2.

segments.speaker: Move As One Coalition Representative Ysabel Eugene G. Agregado
segments.text: Ang lumabas po sa NEP ay zero.

segments.speaker: Move As One Coalition Representative Ysabel Eugene G. Agregado
segments.text: So ngayon po meron po tayong 10 na operational, dalawa po nire-repair ngayon so 8 lang po talaga na trainsets ang nagra-run po from recto all the way to antipolo.

segments.speaker: Move As One Coalition Representative Ysabel Eugene G. Agregado
segments.text: So from the 18 original, ngayon po 10 na lang, dalawa po doon sa 10 na yun ay again inaayos po so 8 lang po ang running ngayon.

segments.speaker: Move As One Coalition Representative Ysabel Eugene G. Agregado
segments.text: So imagine po, nagiging more than 10 minutes na headway pero even if 10 minutes yung frequency nung trains, hindi pa po sigurado kung makakapasok ka.

segments.text: Ang sinabi po nga nila, yung Betty Govel Monte Station na dati po ay wala masyadong tao, ang haba na po ng pila ngayon.

segments.text: For the NSCR, Metro Manila Subway, ito po yung nabanggit na ito po yung pinaka nakaranas po ng pinaka mataas na cuts among all department foreign assisted projects.

segments.speaker: Move As One Coalition Representative Ysabel Eugene G. Agregado
segments.text: Yung 19 billion po ang nabawas for the Metro Manila Subway and 15 billion ang nabawas for the NSCR.

segments.speaker: Move As One Coalition Representative Ysabel Eugene G. Agregado
segments.text: Alam po natin ilang billions na ang nababayad because we have been delaying these projects in interest payments, in commitment fees tama po.

segments.speaker: Move As One Coalition Representative Ysabel Eugene G. Agregado
segments.text: So ito po yung sana makorect ng Senate dahil ito po yung kinot ng House after they passed the budget.

segments.speaker: Move As One Coalition Representative Ysabel Eugene G. Agregado
segments.text: This will delay the NSCR and the Metro Manila Subway back.

segments.text: Next po, tinatawag ko po ang aming road safety advocate na si Lou Hepuela to share a bit on road safety, and then mamaya po si Doc Mau.

segments.speaker: Move As One Coalition Representative Ysabel Eugene G. Agregado
Move As One Coalition Road Safety Advocate Lou Hepuela
Move As One Coalition Road Safety Advocate Lou Hepuela

Move As One Coalition Road Safety Advocate Lou Hepuela
segments.text: Ako po si Lou Hepuela, road safety advocate for Move Us One Coalition.

segments.speaker: Move As One Coalition Road Safety Advocate Lou Hepuela
segments.text: Every third Sunday po noong November.

segments.speaker: Move As One Coalition Road Safety Advocate Lou Hepuela
segments.text: Bate po sa RA 11468, mayroon po tayong National Day of Remembrance for road crash victims, survivors, and their families.

segments.speaker: Move As One Coalition Road Safety Advocate Lou Hepuela
segments.text: Ngayon, ang tanong po, sino po ang in-charge sa road safety sa Pilipinas?

segments.speaker: Move As One Coalition Road Safety Advocate Lou Hepuela
segments.text: Per administrative order po ni PGMA, dahil binuwag po niya yung National Road Safety Committee, which was a cabinet-level committee meeting every so often on road safety,

segments.speaker: Move As One Coalition Road Safety Advocate Lou Hepuela
segments.text: ang nangyayari po ngayon ay si DOTR ang may responsibility sa road safety.

segments.speaker: Move As One Coalition Road Safety Advocate Lou Hepuela
Move As One Coalition Road Safety Advocate Lou Hepuela
segments.text: Last year po, 2025, May, road safety month, tinalaga po ni then-Secretary Vince Dizon ang Task Force Road Safety.

segments.speaker: Move As One Coalition Road Safety Advocate Lou Hepuela
segments.text: Ngayon, naulit na po, since he's now Transportation Secretary, yung problema na po dito, ang mga naka-assign na tao for Task Force Road Safety, busy rin po sila sa Public Transport Modernization Program.

segments.speaker: Move As One Coalition Road Safety Advocate Lou Hepuela
segments.text: Yung problema po dito, hindi po pwede part-time nagtatrabaho sa road safety.

segments.speaker: Move As One Coalition Road Safety Advocate Lou Hepuela
Move As One Coalition Road Safety Advocate Lou Hepuela
segments.text: marvellous document called the PRSAP, the Philippine Road Safety Action Plan, 2023 to 2028, eh 2026 na po.

segments.speaker: Move As One Coalition Road Safety Advocate Lou Hepuela
segments.text: Galaw pagong po ang action sa action plan na yan, kasi wala pong funding for road safety for the past three years.

segments.speaker: Move As One Coalition Road Safety Advocate Lou Hepuela
segments.text: Which is why we ask the Senate, please, kung seryoso po talaga tayo in helping in preventing road crashes, in making sure that our most vulnerable are protected,

segments.speaker: Move As One Coalition Road Safety Advocate Lou Hepuela
segments.text: please, please fund road safety. Thank you po.

segments.speaker: Move As One Coalition Co-convener Dr. Maureen Mata
segments.text: May atas ko naman po, sorry, for MOVA's one po, the Accessibility and Inclusion.

segments.speaker: Move As One Coalition Co-convener Dr. Maureen Mata
segments.text: Hello po, Sen. JV, Sen. Ping, and Sen. Win.

segments.speaker: Move As One Coalition Co-convener Dr. Maureen Mata
segments.text: Iko-connect ko lang po sa nabanggit ni Jibel at sa kanilo.

segments.speaker: Move As One Coalition Co-convener Dr. Maureen Mata
segments.text: Pag hindi po accessible ang ating kalsada, ang ating sasakyan, ang ating infrastructure, definitely road crashes happen.

segments.speaker: Move As One Coalition Co-convener Dr. Maureen Mata
segments.text: Isa po sa datos natin na nagkakaroon ng physical disability ang mga tao ay dahil po sa road.

segments.speaker: Move As One Coalition Co-convener Dr. Maureen Mata
segments.text: So, dagdag na naman po ito sa datos ng tao may kapansanan.

segments.speaker: Move As One Coalition Co-convener Dr. Maureen Mata
segments.text: At nabanggit po ni Dr. Elisa kanina na in our entire life cycle mula bata hanggang tayo ay nakatatanda, tayo po ay makaka-experience ng kapansanan.

segments.speaker: Move As One Coalition Co-convener Dr. Maureen Mata
segments.text: Lalong-lalo na kung tayo po ay nakaka-experience or interact ng different barriers na nakikita po natin like for example, Mount Kamuning.

segments.speaker: Move As One Coalition Co-convener Dr. Maureen Mata
segments.text: Siguro simulan lang, dagdagan ko rin lang na mobility and connectivity is very important.

segments.speaker: Move As One Coalition Co-convener Dr. Maureen Mata
segments.text: Nabanggit po ng lahat dito, accessible, having an accessible health services, accessible education, lahat po accessible.

segments.speaker: Move As One Coalition Co-convener Dr. Maureen Mata
segments.text: Pero gaano ba ka-accessible ito kung may mga naiiwan?

segments.speaker: Move As One Coalition Co-convener Dr. Maureen Mata
segments.text: Lalo na sa 12.9 million persons with disabilities na hindi lamang po sa Imperial Manila manggagaling.

segments.speaker: Move As One Coalition Co-convener Dr. Maureen Mata
segments.text: Manggagaling po ito sa 18 regions natin sa buong Pilipinas.

segments.speaker: Move As One Coalition Co-convener Dr. Maureen Mata
segments.text: Saka sa pinupuntahan po namin, isla pa po ito, ultimo ambulansya na pag may sakit po yung tao may kapansanan,
